issues.summary: Application launch test could intercept the concurrent GPU detector through a shared stdlib Popen mock.
issues.steps_to_reproduce: Previous main CI 37135472914 / job 111239011054 records a second Popen call for Win32_VideoController inside the launch fixture.
issues.expected: The fixture mocks only its intended dependency and preserves background hardware checks.
issues.actual: The old test globally changed subprocess.Popen through an imported module alias.
issues.risk: Flaky unrelated process calls and false CI failure.
issues.resolution: Rebind the desktop module dependency to a private copied namespace. Assert the shared stdlib Popen identity stays unchanged and retain exact approval/launch arguments. Production launch permissions are unchanged.

issues.summary: Immediate low-RAM cancellation left a suspended venv child outside snapshot-based cleanup.
issues.steps_to_reproduce: The 1065-test/62-subtest run passed, then CIM showed PID 18812 from test_host_ram_margin_stops_fixture still suspended with zero CPU after its launcher had exited.
issues.expected: Actual process-family shutdown precedes successful cleanup and lease release.
issues.actual: A logical empty owner snapshot did not prove that a child created during launcher startup was gone.
issues.risk: Residual suspended workers after early cancellation; falsely complete cleanup. Native GUI Builder acceptance must also prove bounded launch latency.
issues.resolution: Extend the existing owners with one low-level Windows Job utility. Create the root suspended, assign its private kill-on-close Job, then resume its single initial thread. The initial thread list comes from the existing psutil native per-process query; the prior per-thread Python Toolhelp walk caused multi-second launch delays while Qt painted. Preserve the exact process/thread identity and suspension checks. Reap and observe the complete Job, including children of an exited launcher. Existing Kernel, permissions, leases, pools and resource guards remain authoritative; non-Windows process groups stay in place.
issues.regression_test: Five real Windows tests: twelve immediate venv cancellations, surviving-child cleanup, unrelated-process preservation, failed assignment before command execution, and holder crash after assignment.
issues.remaining_constraint: Standard Popen cannot atomically supply the Windows job-list startup attribute. Abrupt termination in the tiny interval between suspended creation and Job assignment remains unvalidated. Unusual initial thread layouts or denied Job assignment fail closed. This is not a general crash-proof-process guarantee.

issues.summary: Worker cyclic garbage collection overlapped Python QIconEngine painting during long native Research runs.
issues.steps_to_reproduce: Run scripts/demo_phase10_workspaces.py --native under Python 3.14.2. Crashes observed with PySide6 6.11.2 and 6.12.0. The latter faulthandler trace records cyclic GC in an interactive worker and the GUI inside the custom icon paint callback.
issues.expected: Long-running real Research work remains stable while the GUI paints and workers allocate.
issues.actual: Windows access violation ended both processes before final evidence/cleanup. A bare-button 15-second stress fixture passed and does not reproduce or disprove the full-window failure.
issues.risk: Process crash and loss of unsaved UI state; existing experiment checkpoints remain resumable.
issues.resolution: Candidate removes the Python QIconEngine virtual callback. Original authored vectors render into bounded, high-DPI native QIcon backing pixmaps; Qt paints buttons using native value objects. Retain the Python proxy style owner explicitly on QApplication. No global GC suppression or dependency upgrade. Cause attribution remains provisional until current-source full native Research acceptance passes.
issues.regression_test: Focused DPI/mode/cache checks plus actual current-source native Research master workflow; full regression and matching package/install gates remain pending.

issues.summary: Periodic result reads decoded all 10000 stored runs before trimming to 500, retaining SQLite readers during that work.
issues.steps_to_reproduce: Native 10000-run attempt e6946c4208 stored all 10000 results but timed out delivering the result view; reopening that completed checkpoint failed its verified recorded calculation with database is locked. The database was in DELETE journal mode.
issues.expected: UI result reads and independent verified writes proceed concurrently in the existing local shared database.
issues.actual: A result read took 29.59 seconds during active UI use; idle read of the identical 10000 stored rows took 0.098 seconds. The next recorded write failed after 23 seconds.
issues.risk: Delayed results, occupied interactive worker and failed recorded calculations.
issues.resolution: Extend the existing VirtualLaboratory.get with optional SQL result limits and parameterized casefold search over displayed columns. Count all matches but decode at most 500 visible runs. Fetch raw rows and close read cursors before JSON decoding, releasing the shared database for established knowledge writers. Full exports keep their complete default. A WAL experiment did not resolve the stall and was removed: the bundled SQLite 3.50.4 precedes the upstream WAL-reset fix. No journal-mode migration or runtime upgrade ships.
issues.regression_test: Actual completed experiment tests verify page size, total counts, Unicode/literal SQL-safe filtering beyond the first page and complete exports. A paused JSON decoder requires an independent existing knowledge writer to commit, proving that read locks have been released. Fresh native master/full suite/package/install acceptance remains pending.
issues.remaining_constraint: Filtered counts still scan this bounded experiment table; physical network storage and arbitrary large custom result payloads remain unvalidated. SQLite keeps its prior journal mode; this change does not certify databases manually configured for vulnerable WAL runtimes.

issues.summary: A raw Security fixture targeted a venv redirector; its suspended interpreter child survived the correctly scoped exact-PID termination.
issues.steps_to_reproduce: The first 1077-test/62-subtest final suite passed, but CIM found PID 17168, created at 09:05:19.464 UTC, one suspended thread and parent PID 7324. The Security fixture action journal proves that PID 7324 was the exact approved and verified termination target.
issues.expected: A single-PID containment fixture owns one actual process and leaves no unrelated redirector child.
issues.actual: The production containment contract correctly terminated only the approved PID. The test launched a venv redirector and did not own its suspended child for cleanup.
issues.risk: Test-process leakage and falsely clean test-environment claims. Expanding production termination to a family would exceed exact-PID authorization.
issues.resolution: Launch the base Python interpreter directly in the two exact-PID Security fixtures and their benchmark. Preserve all denial, wrong-start-time, containment approval and verified termination assertions. Reap only the previously recorded suspended fixture after matching PID, creation time, command, parent and thread state. No application/permission implementation changes.
issues.regression_test: The two real OS Security tests pass with direct single-process targets. The complete suite must be rerun with a post-run actual OS process inventory.

issues.summary: Four fixtures assumed canonical-path formatting or a coincidental independent-task start order.
issues.steps_to_reproduce: Commit f4d30cf, CI run 38714805211 / job 116354784850: 1073 tests and 62 subtests pass. Updater expected RUNNER~1 instead of runneradmin; the warm-model mock used resolve rather than normcase(abspath); partial cancellation raced an unfinished echo; foreground ordering relied on coincident timestamps/random IDs.
issues.expected: Fixtures use actual interfaces and explicit causal/admission preconditions across host clocks and Windows path aliases.
issues.actual: Production updater canonicalization, exact reported-model identity and graph ordering functioned as declared; fixture assumptions differed.
issues.risk: False CI failures or an inadvertently shared stdlib Popen mock.
issues.resolution: Expect canonical updater launch paths, isolate updater/llama subprocess dependencies in private namespaces, return the actual provider path-normalization contract, require a completed predecessor through real dependencies, and supply explicit FIFO ages for foreground admission. No production scheduler, permission, model identity or deadlines change.
issues.regression_test: 120 focused tests and the fresh complete 1077-test/62-subtest suite pass in 398.39 seconds with a clean actual OS inventory. Observe the follow-up GitHub CI result after push; runtime application bytes are unchanged.
